reviews.author: Sierbahnn
reviews.content:
You can hide a lot in the dark.
There have been several movies about tour boats getting stranded and its tourist complement getting eaten by local wildlife. There are sharks, there are piranhas, there are alligators, there are even frankenfish. This movie has a hippo. That's novel. It's very cute. I like the premise of it and the characters are engaging enough for there to be actual tension, which is great. The casting is fine, not outstanding, but certainly not lacking. And the direction is perfectly serviceable. The hippo is not as good as one would like, and they hide a lot of that by putting it in low light. That might make it more atmospheric for some, but for me it just looks a bit cheap. It's strange how much better movies like Jurassic Park looked so many years ago when the advance of technology is so swift. I'm guessing the artistry just isn't there. Of course, this movie is nowhere near as well budgeted as Jurassic Park, but it only has the one hippo. So it shouldn't be that much of a stretch to actually make it look scary. I still enjoyed the movie and I will recommend it for "tour boats getting stranded and tourist eaten"- aficionados.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Lost in the treacherous Louisiana swamplands, a group of holidaymakers finds themselves hunted by a vicious, rampaging hippo.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: A relaxing vacation turns into a terrifying fight for survival when a group of holidaymakers gets hopelessly lost in the Louisiana bayou. As they navigate the dense, unfamiliar swamplands, they realize they are being stalked by an unnaturally aggressive, escaped hippopotamus. Isolated from civilization with limited supplies, the group must band together to outsmart the lethal predator. Every attempt to signal for help only seems to draw the territorial beast closer.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: What was supposed to be a scenic getaway quickly devolves into a nightmare when a group of holidaymakers takes a wrong turn and ends up deep within the uncharted Louisiana swamplands. Unbeknownst to them, a massive and unusually aggressive hippopotamus has escaped captivity and claimed the dense marshlands as its supreme hunting ground. Disoriented and stripped of reliable navigation, the group struggles through murky waters and dense vegetation, completely unaware of the threat looming beneath the surface. Terror strikes suddenly when the apex herbivore launches a brutal ambush, instantly shattering any hope of a peaceful rescue. As night falls over the swamp, tensions skyrocket within the group as panic and differing survival instincts threaten to tear them apart from within. Forced to adapt to a lethal environment, they must improvise weapons and craft crude shelters while trying to avoid the beast's relentless attacks. Each attempt to find a way back to safety leads them deeper into the hippo's territorial domain, turning every splash in the water into a potential death sentence. With their numbers dwindling and fear taking hold, the remaining survivors are forced into a desperate, high-stakes showdown against an unstoppable force of nature. Ultimately, they must find a way to outsmart the wild animal before they all succumb to the horrors of the swamp.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Hungry is a high-tension thrill ride that blends survival drama with creature-feature horror. Set against the atmospheric and oppressive backdrop of the Louisiana bayou, the narrative follows a vacationing group whose trip takes a deadly turn after becoming stranded in unfamiliar territory. Rather than standard swamp hazards, they are confronted by an unexpected and utterly terrifying apex threat: a rogue, rampaging hippo. The film explores themes of human vulnerability, team dynamics under extreme pressure, and the raw power of nature as the group relies on grit and quick thinking to stay alive against an unpredictable predator.
